evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.18: sī secus est, commūne errātum est
terms.comment: A mistake one has made, in a fact or in conduct. To make a mistake is errāre or peccāre (Traupman 155); by mistake, imprūdēns or perperam (Traupman 104).

terms.gloss: a mistake in writing, a slip
evidence: Cic. Att. 2.7.5: Castriciānum mendum nōs corrigēmus
terms.comment: The mistake in a written text, a copy or an account, and so in schoolwork: mendum admittere, to make one (Traupman 29). The feminine menda is the same word, used so after Augustus (Suet. Aug. 87, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Suet. Aug. 88.1: commūnis hominum error est
terms.comment: Properly a wandering; then a going astray from the truth, a mistaken belief.

evidence: Traupman 247: vitium facere, to make a mistake
terms.comment: A defect; in the grammarians the faults of speech, barbarisms and solecisms.

evidence: Publ. P 62: Peccātum extenuat, quī celeriter corrigit.
terms.comment: A fault of any kind; in church Latin a sin (see sin).

evidence: Traupman 107: a slip of the tongue, lapsus linguae
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has lapsus in the figurative sense “a failing, error” as rare but classical (Cic. Ac. 1.45), but not the phrase with linguae.

phrases.latin: errāstī, Lupe, littera sed ūnā: nam quō tempore praedium dedistī, māllem tū mihi prandium dedissēs
phrases.english: You made a mistake, Lupus, but only by one letter: when you gave me a farm (praedium), I’d rather you had given me lunch (prandium)

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī
phrases.english: every one of us makes mistakes; we’re human, not gods
I’ll correct the mistake in Castricius’s account
to make a mistake, commit an error
